applies_why: The judge is resolving a pressed link on Matthew 1:16, so K-C governs whether it weighs that collision by chain footing or by the verse alone.
quote: UNDERDETERMINED -- the passive egennēthē (was born) with feminine hēs (of whom) admits both the withheld-father and the birth-narration readings
rule_words: When the witnesses pressed against a link are the pressing side's own chain read together, the collision weighs chain against chain by footing, never verse by verse; that no one of them states the contrary in its own words is the stating-verse test DG-61 retires, at a judge's seat as at a debater's, for either side.
room: ‘weighs chain against chain by footing, never verse by verse’ — either the judge must resolve the pressed link by comparing the chains' footings, or it may treat the verse's own ambiguity as making the link underdetermined.
why: The judge treats Matthew 1:16 as underdetermined because its own verb and relative pronoun admit two readings, which is verse-by-verse weighing instead of the required chain-against-chain footing.
